newsitem.title: FRANCE: Most French want premier from private sector.
newsitem.headline: Most French want premier from private sector.

text.p: Most French people want President Jacques Chirac to replace unpopular Prime Minister Alain Juppe with someone from the private sector if the centre-right retains power in the coming parliamentary election, a poll said on Tuesday.

The BVA poll, to be published in Thursday's Paris Match magazine, found that just 24 percent want Chirac to name a prime minister from either his Gaullist RPR party or the centrist UDF, the governing coalition's junior partner.
Fifty-three percent said Chirac should replace Juppe with someone unconnected with the state, as did General de Gaulle when he called on banker Georges Pompidou.
The remaining 23 percent had no opinion.

The survey found voters warming a bit to Chirac and Juppe ahead of the May 25-June 1 election, with 40 percent having a favourable view of the president's performance and 30 percent approving of Juppe's job as prime minister, both up five percent from a comparable survey last month.

But just 23 percent found Juppe a convincing campaigner compared to 35 percent for Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin, 22 percent for Communist leader Robert Hue, 20 percent for UDF head Francois Leotard and 24 percent for Gaullist former prime minister Edouard Balladur.
The poll findings were based on interviews with 1,075 registered voters conducted last Friday and Saturday.
